pages.text: Alcubierre's metric moves a bubble of flat space by contracting space ahead of it and expanding it behind, at any speed v. Its wall needs negative energy, growing as v²R²σ for radius R and wall sharpness σ; the tidal shear across the wall goes as vσ; a wall that is thick for its bubble (Rσ small) is not a bubble at all.
$(thing)Set$(): Bubble speed, Bubble radius, Wall sharpness σ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Casimir supply: the negative energy needed varies by ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): More negative energy than the forge can hold.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Smaller bubbles form faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Negative energy: E ∝ −v²R²σ$(br)Wall shear: ∝ vσ$(br)Wall thinness: Rσ
